title: ninebark green lane panel deck
instruction:
You are Otto Sundqvist, the compliance officer supporting Ninebark Port Authority's tenant advisory panel. The harbor commission wants the panel to vote in September on a voluntary green-lane program before the next tariff year: participating tenants would receive pre-cleared cargo documentation in exchange for defined open-book audit access. Frida Zubair, who chairs the panel and runs Marrowbone Terminals, has already told commissioners that the proposal sounds like a data grab, so I need one presentation that can win the four largest tenants without overselling the evidence and without relying on a rebuttal round. Use `green_lane_case_register.xlsx` and `green_lane_governing_policy.docx` as the complete source set. Replay the supplied program history and compliance events under the governing policy, compare the two reporting periods, and compare the named jurisdictional requirements in the evidence. The deck must show which four tenants are in scope, the period-over-period material changes, the evidence behind any claimed dwell-time benefit, and a clear distinction between observed results and projections from other ports. Put the concession about transferability on slide two rather than burying it. Answer Frida's audit-access objection in the deck itself by stating the exact record scope, retention period, access boundaries, treatment of confidential material, review outcome categories, and what happens after an adverse finding. Include a compact source or method note that lets another compliance professional reproduce the status and figures, including how overlapping records and the retired helper field were handled. Make the recommendation and the panel decision requested explicit, identify material risks and mitigations, and do not invent benefits, tenants, jurisdictions, or policy requirements that are not supported by the sources. Write the finished presentation to the top level of the working directory, using exactly `Ninebark_Green_Lane_Panel_Deck.pptx`; do not return a second file.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/green_lane_case_register.xlsx` — Opening program state and dated compliance, tenant, audit, and performance events for the two reporting periods and the named jurisdictions.
- `references/green_lane_governing_policy.docx` — The governing policy and comparison extracts that define deterministic status transitions, tenant eligibility, audit scope, retention, confidentiality handling, adverse-finding actions, jurisdictional requirements, and approved terminology.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `Ninebark_Green_Lane_Panel_Deck.pptx` — A decision-ready green-lane program pitch and investigation case file for the tenant advisory panel. (Use only facts, figures, terminology, and policy requirements supported by the two supplied files.; Include the transferability concession on slide two.; Address audit-access scope, retention, confidentiality, outcome categories, and adverse-finding actions in the deck.; Include a reproducible source or method note.; The deck must be readable in a live panel presentation and must not rely on speaker notes for material conclusions.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

materials.text:
Ninebark Port Authority — Green-Lane Governing Policy
Effective for the voluntary tenant green-lane program and the September panel decision before the next tariff year.
1. Status replay and event control
Begin with the supplied opening-state records. Do not infer an opening state from the first dated event.
De-duplicate event rows on the key Tenant ID + Event Type + Effective Date + Reference ID. One key is one event.
Replay events in Effective Date order; on the same date, apply Application, Pre-clearance, Audit, Finding, Remediation, then Status Change.
Approved tenant statuses are Pending, Active, Suspended, and Closed. A qualifying application approval moves Pending to Active. An Adverse audit finding moves Active to Suspended. A completed corrective-action follow-up with a Clear or Conditional outcome may move Suspended to Active.
The retired field Status Helper is non-authoritative. The opening state plus cleaned event replay controls final status and outcome.
2. Scope, periods, eligibility, and materiality
The four largest tenants are the four highest 2024 cargo-volume records in the opening state: Marrowbone Terminals, Gildenhall Logistics, Overbrook Energy, and Pellinore Foods.
Earlier reporting period: 2024-01-01 through 2024-06-30. Later reporting period: 2025-01-01 through 2025-06-30. A qualifying tenant is counted once per period using Tenant ID + Period.
Principal performance metric is average dwell time in hours for Ninebark observations, using the cleaned observation rows. A change of at least 1.0 hour in absolute value is material.
Ninebark observations are measured results. Other-port observations may be shown only as external observations or projections and are not Ninebark results.
3. Audit access terms
Record scope: participating-tenant green-lane cargo documentation, pre-clearance decisions, shipment-level exception logs, and remediation evidence for the audited period.
Retention: seven years from the relevant shipment or decision date.
Access boundary: Ninebark Port Authority compliance officers and the tenant's designated audit liaison may use a secure read-only export or supervised on-site review; no unrestricted production-system access.
Commercially sensitive material is segregated or redacted where it is not needed for the compliance determination, shared under confidentiality obligations, and used only for program oversight.
Approved audit outcomes are Clear, Conditional, and Adverse. After an Adverse finding: issue written notice, suspend pre-clearance, require a corrective-action plan within 30 calendar days, and conduct a follow-up review. Reinstatement requires a subsequent Clear or Conditional outcome.
4. Jurisdiction comparison
Northbank: seven-year record retention, secure audit access to the defined green-lane record scope, and confidentiality controls. These requirements apply to the voluntary Ninebark program.
Eastmere: five-year retention and regulator notice within 10 business days for reportable incidents. Eastmere requirements are contextual and do not apply to this voluntary program unless a shipment is subject to Eastmere oversight.
5. Approved panel language
Use “voluntary pilot,” “pre-clearance,” “audit access,” and the status/outcome vocabulary above. The panel decision is “Approve,” “Approve with conditions,” or “Do not approve.”

spec.professional_context: Ninebark Port Authority is preparing a voluntary tenant green-lane program before the next tariff year. The compliance case file must help the tenant advisory panel decide whether the proposed pre-clearance and audit-access terms are credible, bounded, and worth adopting.
difficulty_sources: replay a supplied opening program state through a dated event log using the governing policy
compare two reporting periods and two named jurisdictions while preserving source traceability
identify and de-duplicate overlapping source records without relying on a stale retired helper column
turn a multi-stage compliance analysis into a concise decision deck for a skeptical stakeholder audience

semantic_content: An opening-state table for the green-lane program with synthetic tenant identifiers and organization names including Marrowbone Terminals, Gildenhall Logistics, and Overbrook Energy.

A dated event log covering an earlier and a later reporting period. Events include tenant applications, document-pre-clearance results, audit-access actions, findings, remediation, and program-status changes.
Period metrics for the four largest tenants and comparator port observations, with enough source fields to distinguish observed Ninebark results from projections or external observations.
Evidence identifying the two jurisdictions to compare and linking jurisdiction-specific requirements to the policy document.
layout_requirements: Place a visible banner block above the principal table and one or more gutter columns to its left so the real table does not begin at A1.

Include one retired helper column with stale values that conflict with the status derivable from the governing policy and event history. Label it as retired in the source, but do not make its values authoritative.

Include overlapping duplicate event rows sharing the exact de-duplication key stated in the governing policy. The duplicate rows must be identical or overlapping in a way that would inflate counts or alter a replay if retained.
Do not introduce blanks, formula errors, contradictory source facts, malformed dates, unit ambiguities, or any other seeded standard defect.

semantic_content: Define the deterministic event de-duplication key and event precedence or replay rules.
Define the opening state, valid status transitions, effective-date handling, and how later remediation or adverse findings affect status.
Define the eligibility rule for the four largest tenants, the period comparison basis, and the material-change threshold.
Define the exact audit record scope, retention period, access boundary, confidential-material treatment, review outcome categories, and actions following an adverse finding.
Provide the named jurisdictional requirements for comparison and indicate which requirements are applicable to the voluntary program.
State which metrics are observed Ninebark results, which are external-port observations, and which may be presented only as projections or illustrative evidence.
Identify the retired helper field as non-authoritative and state that the event log and policy-derived replay control the final status.
Provide approved labels or terminology for status, audit outcomes, and the panel decision so the deck can use consistent wording.
construction_constraints: Use explicit deterministic rules rather than unresolved judgment calls.
Make all facts needed for the rubric text-extractable.
Ensure the policy and workbook are mutually consistent after duplicate removal and replay.

transformation.stage_1: Locate the real tables despite the banner and gutter, identify the authoritative fields, and exclude the retired helper column.
transformation.stage_2: De-duplicate events on the policy-stated key and replay the cleaned event log from the supplied opening state.
transformation.stage_3: Derive final tenant statuses, audit outcomes, period comparisons, material changes, jurisdiction comparisons, and the distinction between observed and projected benefits.
transformation.stage_4: Select the four largest tenants under the policy definition and present the resulting investigation and bounded recommendation in a concise decision deck.

gold_derivation.method: Use an offline reference script or independently checked workbook logic to parse the authoritative table, remove duplicate keys, ignore the retired helper field, replay events according to the policy, and calculate every reported figure from the cleaned state.
numeric_rules: Every total, count, percentage, status, and period comparison in the rubric is derived from the supplied sources after de-duplication and replay.
Use the policy's stated material-change threshold and rounding convention.
Use the policy's stated denominator and treatment for any zero-duration or otherwise non-comparable observation; the sources must provide the required convention.
External-port dwell-time observations must never be presented as measured Ninebark savings.
gold_derivation.intended_verdict: A strong deck supports a bounded voluntary pilot or recommendation only to the extent permitted by the replayed policy state and evidence, plainly concedes the transferability limitation, and answers the audit-access objection with the exact policy controls.

reference_files.purpose: Opening program state and dated compliance, tenant, audit, and performance events for the two reporting periods and the named jurisdictions.
reference_files.discovery: Inspect the workbook visually and programmatically; the real tables are below a banner and to the right of gutter columns. Follow the source headers and policy document rather than assuming the first row or column is data.

reference_files.purpose: The governing policy and comparison extracts that define deterministic status transitions, tenant eligibility, audit scope, retention, confidentiality handling, adverse-finding actions, jurisdictional requirements, and approved terminology.
reference_files.discovery: Read the document as the governing source. It states the de-duplication key and identifies a retired helper field whose values are not authoritative.

deliverables.description: A decision-ready green-lane program pitch and investigation case file for the tenant advisory panel.
constraints: Use only facts, figures, terminology, and policy requirements supported by the two supplied files.
Include the transferability concession on slide two.
Address audit-access scope, retention, confidentiality, outcome categories, and adverse-finding actions in the deck.
Include a reproducible source or method note.
The deck must be readable in a live panel presentation and must not rely on speaker notes for material conclusions.
